findings.finding: SignalPolicy.evaluate_probabilities is the single policy chokepoint. findings.topic: Model vs Strategy independence — can model BUY while strategy says NO_TRADE?
findings.finding: YES, the model can independently signal BUY while the strategy gates produce NO_TRADE. The model confidence is ONE input to SignalPolicy. Multiple independent gates can convert a BUY-class proposal to NO_TRADE: (1) HTF misalignment (model bullish but h4_trend<0), (2) SR resistance margin fail, (3) confidence gate (model confidence < threshold), (4) zone quality gate, (5) anti-flip, (6) same-level re-entry lockout. The model prediction enters via probs[1] (BUY prob) but the policy can and frequently does emit NO_TRADE despite a BUY signal from inference.

findings.topic: Strategy can trade independently of model
findings.finding: YES — RuleMatrixEngine.evaluate_pre_trade_entry() at signals/rule_matrix.py:491-551 operates as an INDEPENDENT strategy layer. It evaluates raw market microstructure signals (FVG sniper fill, Judas swing fade, order block tap, wick absorption, flash momentum, OFI reversal, news spike, etc.) with hardcoded confidences (0.80-0.95) and returns TradeProposals WITHOUT consulting model probabilities at all. RuleMatrix entries bypass the model confidence gate entirely.

findings.topic: Model can trade independently of strategy
findings.finding: NO — the model cannot trade independently. Model inference output (probs from InferenceService.infer_probabilities) flows ONLY through SignalPolicy.evaluate_probabilities, which ALWAYS runs the full strategy gate chain (HTF alignment, SR alignment, zone quality, anti-flip, re-entry lockout, confidence gates). The model's directional BUY/SELL must pass every strategy gate to become a proposal. Even high-confidence model BUYs are rejected by HTF_TREND_FILTER or CONFIDENCE_GATE without strategy agreement. SMC_GOD_MODE is the sole bypass, and it still requires strategy-level microstructure confirmation (BOS + OB + sweep + FVG).

findings.topic: Execution assumptions and parity (paper vs live)

findings.topic: Three State Machines and Governance Contradiction
findings.finding: Three separate, parallel state machines govern model status across subsystems with divergent vocabularies: 1) ModelStatus in model_lifecycle (CANDIDATE, CHALLENGER, CHAMPION, REJECTED, ARCHIVED, INVALID), 2) PromotionState in governance (RESEARCH, VALIDATED, CHALLENGER, SHADOW, READY_FOR_REVIEW, APPROVED, CHAMPION, REJECTED, RETIRED), 3) LabStatus in model_lab (CREATED, TRAINING, COMPLETED, FAILED, REJECTED, VALIDATED, PROMOTION_CANDIDATE). Because they persist in different tables/databases, states can become contradictory (e.g. a model marked CHALLENGER in model_lifecycle may be RESEARCH or VALIDATED in governance).

findings.topic: MT5 Platform Support and OS Constraints
findings.finding: The native MetaTrader5 Python package is WINDOWS-ONLY (win32). On Linux, import MetaTrader5 fails and sys.platform != win32 sets HAS_NATIVE_MT5 = False (adapters/mt5/mt5_adapter.py:71-79). For Linux/Docker environments, NSE provides RemoteMT5GatewayAdapter (connecting over network to a Windows MT5 host) and PaperAdapter (simulated execution). Native MT5 execution on Linux is UNSUPPORTED; Remote and Paper adapters are PRODUCTION CAPABILITIES.
